newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NIGERIAN KANU GIVEN GO-AHEAD TO PLAY AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIAN KANU GIVEN GO-AHEAD TO PLAY AGAIN.

text.p: Inter's 20-year-old Nigerian attacker Nwankwo Kanu has been cleared by doctors to return to professional soccer after heart surgery in the United States five months ago, the Italian club said on Friday.
Inter said they had received a news release from the Cleveland Clinic in Ohio earlier on Friday detailing the African player of the year's condition and progress.

"Five months after undergoing surgery to repair a deformed aortic heart valve, Nigerian soccer star Nwankwo Kanu was told by physicians at the Cleveland Clinic today that he can return to professional soccer," said the hospital statement.
It quoted cardiologist John R. Kramer as saying that the surgery on Kanu had been successful.
"Based on the results of metabolic stress testing this week, we are removing all limitations and allowing him to return to full normal activities, including his professional activities," Kramer said.
"He is stronger now physically than he was before the operation," he added.
Inter welcomed the news while urging continued caution against raising expectations too high.

"FC Internazionale hope that the same optimism on the player's sporting recovery will be supported under the sporting and medical regulations in force in Italy, an optimism that must still be tempered by obvious prudence," it said.

Kanu, who was signed by Inter from Dutch champions Ajax in the summer after helping Nigeria to win the 1996 Olympic soccer tournament, was diagnosed as having congenital heart disease by Inter's doctors before the serie A season started.
They warned that if he carried on playing without an operation he could die.
The Cleveland Clinic said Kanu was born with a deformed aortic valve that had begun to leak, affecting his heart.

The Nigerian went to Ohio for an operation in late November and doctors, attempting to increase his prospects of returning to the sport, decided to surgically repair the defective valve rather than replace it.

Kanu's manager Franklin Sedoc was quoted as saying in the Cleveland statement that the player had been motivated during his rehabilitation by his desire to play professionally again and he now wanted to rejoin his Inter team mates.
"He now looks forward to what we hope will be a long career in professional soccer and to a long and healthy life."
